result.text: Remission at Week 26: 72.3% avacopan vs 70.1% prednisone (treatment difference 3.4%, 95% CI [-6.0%, 12.8%]) — non-inferior. Sustained remission at Week 52: 65.7% vs 54.9% (treatment difference 12.5%, 95% CI [2.6, 22.3]; p=0.013) — superior.

citations.quote: Remission was achieved by 72.3% of patients in the TAVNEOS group and 70.1% of patients in the prednisone group at Week 26 (treatment difference: 3.4%, 95% CI [-6.0%, 12.8%]).

Study CL010_168 met its primary endpoints, demonstrating superiority for sustained remission at Week 52 (avacopan vs. prednisone treatment difference 12.5% with 95% CI [2.6%, 22.3%]). Noninferiority, but not superiority was demonstrated for remission at Week 26 (avacopan vs. prednisone treatment difference 3.4% with 95% CI [-6.0%, 12.8%]).

indication.text: Adjunctive treatment of adult patients with severe active ANCA-associated vasculitis (GPA and MPA) in combination with standard therapy including glucocorticoids; TAVNEOS does not eliminate glucocorticoid use.

citations.quote: TAVNEOS is indicated as an adjunctive treatment of adult patients with severe active anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic autoantibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis (granulomatosis with polyangiitis [GPA] and microscopic polyangiitis [MPA]) in combination with standard therapy including glucocorticoids. TAVNEOS does not eliminate glucocorticoid use.

target_moa.text: Avacopan is a small molecule antagonist of the complement 5a receptor (C5aR), blocking C5a-mediated neutrophil chemoattraction and activation implicated in ANCA-associated vasculitis.

citations.quote: Avacopan is a small molecule antagonist of C5a receptor (C5aR). C5a, the cleaved fragment of C5, is a terminal component of the complement cascade and acts as a potent neutrophil chemoattractant and agonist.
It has been proposed that C5a and C5aR may play a central role in the pathogenesis of anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis (AAV).
Avacopan is a small molecule antagonist of C5a receptor (C5aR).

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥5%): nausea (23.5% vs 20.7%), headache (20.5% vs 14.0%), hypertension (18.1% vs 17.7%), diarrhea, vomiting, rash. Serious hepatic injury and elevated liver function tests occurred more frequently with TAVNEOS; hepatic-related AEs occurred in 13.3% of TAVNEOS patients vs 11.6% of prednisone patients.

citations.quote: The most common adverse reactions (≥5%) are: nausea, headache, hypertension, diarrhea, vomiting, rash, fatigue, upper abdominal pain, dizziness, blood creatinine increased, and paresthesia.

requirement.text: 4155-1: Conduct a randomized controlled clinical trial of at least five years duration in ANCA-associated vasculitis patients to evaluate safety outcomes, including hepatotoxicity/drug-induced liver injury and serious hypersensitivity reactions (angioedema and anaphylaxis).

citations.quote: 4155-1 Conduct a randomized controlled clinical trial of at least five years duration in patients with anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic autoantibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis to evaluate safety outcomes, including hepatotoxicity and drug-induced liver injury, and serious hypersensitivity reactions, including angioedema and anaphylaxis.

requirement.text: 4155-2: Conduct a clinical drug interaction trial evaluating the effect of repeated doses of avacopan 30 mg twice daily with food at steady state on the PK of a sensitive CYP3A4 substrate (e.g., simvastatin).

citations.quote: 4155-2 Conduct a clinical drug interaction trial to evaluate the effect of repeated doses of avacopan 30 mg twice daily with food at steady state on the pharmacokinetics of a sensitive substrate of CYP3A4 (e.g., simvastatin) to inform appropriate dosing strategies for coadministration of avacopan with CYP3A4 substrates.

requirement.text: 4155-3: Conduct a randomized controlled clinical trial of at least five years duration in ANCA-associated vasculitis patients to evaluate efficacy outcomes with long-term avacopan treatment.

summary.text: TAVNEOS (avacopan) was reviewed under a Standard (non-priority) review of NDA 214487, and was granted Orphan Drug designation for ANCA-associated vasculitis. It was not an accelerated approval. An Arthritis Advisory Committee was convened on May 6, 2021, at which the committee was split, and the drug was approved with postmarketing requirements/commitments for long-term safety, efficacy, and drug-interaction studies.
